name: lookahead-brief
title: Look-ahead brief
description: Short look-ahead of a P6 project: activities in progress, starting and finishing in the next weeks, critical ones first, by week of the window, with fixed follow-up actions. Use when the user asks what is coming up, for a look-ahead or for a short-term plan.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: weeks
args.description: Look-ahead length in weeks from the data date (1 to 52)

template:
Look-ahead brief of project {project} for the next {weeks} weeks from the data date: activities in progress, starting, finishing or spanning the window, critical ones first, by week, with fixed follow-up actions. Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. crit = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, critical_only=true, limit=30): critical activities of the window.
2. all = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, limit=50): every activity of the window, weeks, counts, data date.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The categories of an activity can overlap (in progress and finishing). The actions are the fixed sentences
  of report.md only.

# Look-ahead brief of {project}

Window from {window_from} to {window_to} (end excluded): {window_days} calendar days from the data date {data_date}. Last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Dates and float come from that run: open activities use their remaining dates, LOE and WBS summary activities are left out.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and critical flags are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

## In the window

- Activities listed: {listed}.
- In progress: {in_progress}; starting: {starting}; finishing: {finishing}; spanning the whole window: {spanning}.
  These categories overlap (an activity can be in progress and finishing): they do not add up to the activities listed.
- Critical: {critical} ({critical_definition}).

## Weeks

In the tables below, categories are the reasons an activity is listed (in_progress, starting, finishing, spanning); forecast start is the actual start of an activity in progress, else its remaining start; forecast finish is its remaining finish. Start week and finish week are the weeks of the window holding those dates ("outside" when the date is not in the window).

[table: weeks]

## Critical activities

[table: critical]

## All activities of the window

[table: all]

## Actions

[if: critical]
- Review the {critical} critical activities of the window first, with their owners: confirm their forecast dates and what they wait for.
[end if]
[if: in_progress]
- Collect the progress of the {in_progress} activities in progress before the next update: actual dates, remaining duration and percent complete.
[end if]
[if: starting]
- Check that the {starting} activities starting in the window are ready: predecessors finished, crews, materials and permits available.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_lookahead says the project has no data date: repeat its message and stop.
- weeks is not a whole number from 1 to 52: "The look-ahead takes 1 to 52 weeks." and stop.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. crit.data_date = all.data_date = all.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. crit.window.from = all.window.from (same window start).
3. crit.window.to = all.window.to (same window end).
4. crit.total = all.counts.critical (the critical table lists every critical activity counted in the window).

If one differs, the database changed between the calls: run the two calls again once. If it still
differs, say which pair differs and do not publish the counts it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (weeks 13, critical 30, all 50).
  A table whose call has more pages (next_offset not null) ends with its line "Showing the first
  <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers copied from that call.
- Every activity is written "Activity ID - name".
- The category counts overlap (an activity can be in progress and finishing): they are never added up
  or compared with the activities listed.
- Categories are the items of window joined by ", ", in their order. Start week and finish week are
  copied from start_week and finish_week; null is written "outside".
- The warning block is kept only when schedule_state.stale is true; each action is kept only when its
  count is not 0, with no other advice added.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Look-ahead brief

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. crit = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, critical_only=true, limit=30): critical activities of the window.
2. all = p6_lookahead(project="{project}", weeks={weeks}, limit=50): every activity of the window, weeks, counts, data date.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {weeks}: Look-ahead length in weeks from the data date (1 to 52), as given

## Units

- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | all.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the project |
| last_f9 | all.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | all.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | this server changed the project after the last F9 |
| window_from | all.window.from |  | datetime | n/a | start of the window (the data date) |
| window_to | all.window.to |  | datetime | n/a | end of the window, excluded |
| window_days | all.window.days | count | int | n/a | length of the window in calendar days |
| listed | all.total | count | int | n/a | activities of the window (LOE and WBS summary left out) |
| in_progress | all.counts.in_progress | count | int | n/a | activities in progress |
| starting | all.counts.starting | count | int | n/a | not started activities starting in the window |
| finishing | all.counts.finishing | count | int | n/a | open activities finishing in the window |
| spanning | all.counts.spanning | count | int | n/a | not started activities starting before and finishing after the window |
| critical | all.counts.critical | count | int | n/a | critical open activities of the window |
| critical_definition | all.critical_definition |  | text | n/a | the project's definition of critical |

## Table weeks

The weeks of the window: 7 calendar days each from the window start, the last one cut at the window end.

Rows: all.weeks, in the order returned, at most 13 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 13 items, add the line: Only the first 13 weeks are shown.
No rows: write 'No week in the window.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Week | week |  | int | n/a |  |
| From | from |  | datetime | n/a |  |
| To (excluded) | to |  | datetime | n/a |  |

## Table critical

Critical open activities of the window, by forecast start, then finish, then Activity ID.

Rows: crit.rows, in the order returned, at most 30.
When crit.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> critical activities. (returned and total of crit).
No rows: write 'No critical activity in the window.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Categories | window |  | list | n/a |  |
| Forecast start | fcst_start |  | date | n/a |  |
| Forecast finish | fcst_finish |  | date | n/a |  |
| Start week | start_week |  | int | outside |  |
| Finish week | finish_week |  | int | outside |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Critical | critical |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Table all

Every activity of the window, by forecast start, then finish, then Activity ID.

Rows: all.rows, in the order returned, at most 50.
When all.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities. (returned and total of all).
No rows: write 'No activity in the window.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Categories | window |  | list | n/a |  |
| Forecast start | fcst_start |  | date | n/a |  |
| Forecast finish | fcst_finish |  | date | n/a |  |
| Start week | start_week |  | int | outside |  |
| Finish week | finish_week |  | int | outside |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Critical | critical |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date in both look-aheads and the schedule state: crit.data_date = all.data_date = all.schedule_state.data_date
- same window start: crit.window.from = all.window.from
- same window end: crit.window.to = all.window.to
- critical activities listed = critical count of the window: crit.total = all.counts.critical
